EXPORT REGISTRATION RECORD
1. Establishment Details
2. Registered Export Operations

This establishment is registered to conduct export operations for almonds (nut). All export activities carried out at this premises are within the registered scope as approved by the Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF).
3. Registration Status

Registration RE-SA-2020-0155 is current and active. The establishment was granted registration on 3 August 2020 and the current registration period extends to 2 August 2023. There are no conditions, suspensions or reviews attached to this registration.
4. Fit and Proper Person

Raymond Veitch is the nominated responsible person for this registration. The establishment has been under continuous management since 2012. The entity is a proprietary company registered with ASIC. The responsible person has completed the DAFF Export Compliance Fundamentals training and holds current industry accreditation.
5. Registered Premises — Area Description

The registered area is the entire farm property at 44 Port Wakefield Road, Gawler SA 5118, totalling approximately 23.4 hectares. All paddocks, laneways, buildings and infrastructure are included in the registered area.
6. Features, Facilities and Adjoining Sites
6.1 Buildings and Structures
6.2 Services and Utilities
6.3 Adjoining Sites
Standard agricultural land uses on adjoining properties.
7. Layout and Product Flow

A scaled site plan is attached at Appendix A. The plan shows the location of all receival, storage, processing and dispatch infrastructure, including silo positions, shed footprints, hardstand areas, weighbridge, access roads, and the designated export sampling point.

Product flow: almonds is received at the intake pit (north hardstand), elevated to the main conveyor, and directed to either the silo complex or receival shed. Cleaned and graded product is transferred by auger to the outloading hopper for bulk dispatch. All product flow is contained within the registered area. Segregation from non-registered commodities is maintained by dedicated equipment and labelled storage zones.
8. Construction, Equipment and Facilities

The establishment infrastructure is designed and maintained to support the export of almonds. Total storage capacity is approximately 3,500 tonnes. Structures are of steel-frame construction with concrete flooring throughout the grain-contact areas. Maintenance inspections are carried out annually and records held on site.
9. Notification of Changes

No changes to the registered establishment name, address, ownership, management or trading name have occurred since the last registration renewal. Should any such changes occur, DAFF will be notified in writing within the required timeframe as per Rule 4-6 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.
10. Alterations to Registered Premises

No structural alterations or additions to the registered premises have been carried out since the last registration approval. Any proposed alterations will be submitted to DAFF for approval prior to commencement of works, in accordance with Rule 4-5 of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

13. Food Safety Program

A HACCP-based food safety program is maintained for all export operations. The program addresses pre-harvest, receival, storage, processing and dispatch stages. Critical control points are documented with monitoring procedures and corrective action plans. The food safety program is reviewed annually or following any significant operational change.
14. Record Keeping

Records relating to all export operations, including receival dockets, storage logs, treatment records, dispatch documentation and audit reports, are maintained on site and in the business management system. Records are retained for a minimum of two years from the date of the relevant export activity in accordance with Rule 4-7B of the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021.

6. Hygiene and Waste Controls (Checking Point 3.1)

[DEFICIENCY — INADEQUATE / NOT DOCUMENTED FOR THIS ESTABLISHMENT]
This HACCP plan (Version 1.0 — initial registration) does not contain a site-specific hygiene and sanitation program for the Kununurra gin facility.

A generic industry template refers to 'equipment cleaning between runs' but:
• No documented cleaning schedules for the gin stand, lint cleaner, bale press or storage shed.
• No cleaning chemicals specified or approved.
• No personnel hygiene procedures documented.
• No cleaning records (forms) defined or referenced.

ACTION REQUIRED: Develop and document a site-specific Hygiene and Sanitation Program covering: (a) gin equipment cleaning schedule; (b) bale shed cleaning; (c) personnel hygiene requirements; (d) cleaning chemicals approved for use; (e) cleaning verification (swabs or visual inspection); (f) cleaning records retention.

[DEFICIENCY — NOT DOCUMENTED]
Waste management procedures for Clare Valley Vine & Grain Pty Ltd are NOT included in this HACCP plan. No waste streams, disposal methods, frequencies or records are documented.
7. Pest Control (Checking Point 3.2)

Pest Control Program (CLA-PCP-001):
• General pest controls described.
• No formal monitoring schedule or corrective action procedure documented.
• Pest effectiveness cannot be demonstrated without records.
8. Traceability and Integrity (Checking Point 4.1)

Traceability System (KCG-TRACE-001):
• Module receival record: farm ID, paddock, variety, module number, weight.
• Gin batch record: gin run ID, module numbers, bale number range, HVI classing data.
• Bale disposition: bale number → storage location → fumigation batch → dispatch.
• Dispatch docket: bale numbers → container → vessel → destination.
9. Product Flow Chart and Failed Goods (Checking Point 4.1)
Product flow chart: see Section 3 Process Flow Diagram.

Failed Goods Procedure (KCG-FGP-001):
• Pink bollworm positive bales: quarantine; DAFF notification; disinfestation treatment applied.
• Contamination positive bale: quarantine; remove contaminated portion; re-bale if possible; dispose if not.
• Fumigation residue above limit: extend vent; re-test; do not dispatch.
• Non-conformance record maintained.
10. Phytosanitary Security / Contamination Risk (Checking Point 4.2)

Phytosanitary Security (KCG-PSP-001):
• Fumigated export bales stored in sealed shed area; access restricted.
• Bale identification: each bale stencilled with bale number, gin ID and destination.
• Container inspection before loading; seal number recorded on dispatch docket.
• DAFF sampling and phytosanitary certificate issued per consignment.
11. Verification and Record Keeping
Internal audit of HACCP plan: annual, by HACCP team lead.
External audit: DAFF registered establishment audit (periodic).
CCP monitoring records retained minimum 2 years.
HACCP plan reviewed following: product change, process change, new hazard identified, customer complaint, DAFF non-conformance.

FARM MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. OVERVIEW

Gawler River Almonds is a registered export establishment located at 44 Port Wakefield Road, Gawler SA 5118, SA. The establishment holds RE Number RE-SA-2020-0155 and is registered to handle and export Canola under the Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021. This Farm Management Plan documents the physical infrastructure, equipment, facilities, design standards, waste management arrangements and establishment condition relevant to compliance with Chapter 4 of the Rules and the DAFF Performance Standards IMLS-12-3742.
2. BUILDINGS AND INFRASTRUCTURE
Rules s4-2 — buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for export operations
3. EQUIPMENT AND MACHINERY
Rules s4-2(4) — equipment adequate for the type of export operations conducted
4. FACILITIES AND SERVICES
Rules s4-2 — Element 2.1 checking points C1, C2, C3
4.1 Buildings, Equipment and Facilities (C1)

The establishment has all buildings, equipment, facilities and services required for the registered export operations. Facilities are maintained in an operational condition appropriate for handling and exporting Canola.
4.2 Lighting (C2)

High-efficiency LED battens throughout: 470 lux packing hall, 360 lux cool store entry, 342 lux dispatch bay. Sensor-activated step-lighting along conveyor access walkways. All fittings shatterproof-sleeved, IP54 rated minimum.
4.3 Handwashing and Toilet Facilities (C3)

Purpose-built amenities: 1 toilet, 2 hand basins — insulated hot-water system, soap and single-use paper towels. Amenities connected to main processing building via covered walkway. In-line handwash basin at processing floor entry point.
5. DESIGN AND CONSTRUCTION STANDARDS
Rules s4-2(5), s4-2(6) — Element 2.2 checking points C4, C5, C6
5.1 Cleanability (C4)

Purpose-built construction with cleanability designed in: coved epoxy floors, smooth coated-steel wall panels, no horizontal ledges on equipment or structure, all joints sealed with food-grade silicone, recessed floor drain channels with removable SS covers. Annual deep-clean by specialist contractor supplements weekly programme.
5.2 Contamination and Pest Harbourage Minimisation (C5)

Building envelope sealed to export standard: galvanised mesh (6 mm) on all openings; door brush seals replaced every 2 years; expansion joints filled with flexible polyurethane; no open eaves — soffit board sealed to top of wall cladding; all roof penetrations (vents, conduits) flashed and sealed. No horizontal structural members without drainage slope.
5.3 Waste Disposal Design (C6)

Waste disposal: bunded concrete waste pad (4×6 m, 150 mm kerb on 3 sides) adjacent to building for solid waste collection in sealed lidded bins; liquid waste to licensed grease-trap and sewer connection; dust collection by wet scrubber — effluent to contained holding pond; all chemical waste in labelled containers in chemical store for licensed disposal. Records maintained.
6. WASTE MANAGEMENT SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — Element 3.1 checking point C7
6.1 Waste Management Procedures (C7)

Waste Management SOP (WM-SOP-163, version 2.3, current): specifies waste stream segregation, bin placement, collection frequencies and disposal methods. Reviewed bi-annually. Non-conformances logged in the corrective action register. Accessible to all staff on site intranet.
Waste streams and handling arrangements:
7. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION
Rules s4-6 — Element 3.4 (C8) and Element 3.5 (C9)
7.1 Hygiene and Cleanliness (C8)

Internal inspection results: floor — no accumulated debris in corners or wall bases; equipment — all conveyor belts, rollers and hoppers clean; overhead structure — free from hanging debris; drains — clear and odour-free; amenities — clean with full consumable stocks. Last full deep-clean: 4 weeks prior to this assessment.
7.2 Pest Condition (C9)

Current pest status: all monitoring indicators within acceptable range. Rodent bait consumption at routine background level. Insect sticky traps show no grain storage pest species. No evidence of bird entry. Bait station register up to date and signed by licensed pest management technician (last service: January 2025).

HYGIENE & SANITATION MANAGEMENT PLAN
Registered Establishment — Export Control (Plants and Plant Products) Rules 2021
1. ESTABLISHMENT INFORMATION
2. SCOPE AND OBJECTIVES
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — System of controls to manage hygiene and waste at the establishment

This plan covers all areas of Gawler River Almonds used in horticultural packing and cold-chain export operations for Cherries. It applies to all permanent and casual employees, contractors, and visitors on site. The plan is reviewed annually or following any significant change to the establishment or operations.
Objectives of this plan:
Ensure all areas of the establishment are maintained in a clean and hygienic condition.
Prevent contamination of Cherries during handling and export preparation.
Establish clear responsibilities for cleaning activities.
Maintain records that demonstrate ongoing compliance with hygiene requirements.
Support effective pest exclusion through hygienic site conditions.
3. PERSONNEL AND RESPONSIBILITIES
4. MASTER CLEANING SCHEDULE
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — documented system of controls for hygiene (C1, C2)
5. AREA-SPECIFIC CLEANING PROCEDURES (SOPs)
Detailed step-by-step procedures for each area of the establishment
Receival Dock / Unloading Bay

After each produce intake: Remove all packing material (bins, cartons, netting) from dock. Sweep floor of organic debris (leaves, soil, rejected produce). Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Apply to floor with scrubbing brush, allow 3-minute contact time, then rinse with pressure hose ensuring all residue is cleared to drain. Check dock door seals for damage. Sign intake log on completion.
Grading & Sorting Line

After each production run: Power down and isolate grading line before cleaning. Remove produce residue from conveyor belts and rollers manually. Prepare EnzymeClear at 1:20. Apply to belt surfaces, brushes, and rollers. Contact time 5 minutes. Wipe down all surfaces and rinse with clean water. Inspect brushes for wear or product trapping. Restart test run to confirm mechanical function. Record in Grading Log.
Packing Area / Line

End of each shift: Clear all produce from packing tables and conveyor line. Remove used packaging film, cartons, and waste to the external waste bay. Prepare ProClean 200 at 1:50. Wipe packing tables, scales, and conveyor surfaces. Sweep and mop floor. Check under conveyor for accumulation. Packing Supervisor signs shift cleaning record before end of shift.
Cold Storage / Coolrooms

Monthly and between commodity loads: Defrost evaporator coils per manufacturer instructions. Prepare AcidRinse 500 at 1:50. Apply to evaporator surfaces and drain tray to remove mineral scale. Rinse. Prepare QuatSan 100 at 1:100. Wipe all internal wall panels, shelving, and floor. Clear floor drains of accumulated organic material. Record temperature before re-loading. Cold Store Manager signs maintenance log.
Pre-Cool Chamber

Designated staff are responsible for maintaining the Pre-Cool Chamber in a clean and hygienic condition following each production run or daily as scheduled. Appropriate cleaning agents at specified dilutions shall be used. Completed cleaning activities are to be recorded in the site cleaning log.
6. MANAGEMENT OF RESIDUES AND DEAD-STOCK ZONES

Areas prone to organic residue accumulation include floor drain channels, conveyor return runs, and spaces under grading machinery. These areas are cleaned daily or as required to prevent fermentation, mould growth, and pest attraction.
7. APPROVED CLEANING CHEMICAL REGISTER
All chemicals must be used at specified dilutions. Safety Data Sheets (SDS) maintained on site.
8. RECORD-KEEPING SYSTEM
Rules s4-7A(2)(a) — records to demonstrate compliance (C3, C4)
8.1 Record System

Cleaning records are maintained using a combination of paper log sheets and digital entries in the site management system. All records are retained at site for a minimum of two years from the date of completion.
8.2 Sanitation Verification Log Template
9. VERIFICATION PROCEDURES
Independent third-party hygiene audits are conducted twice annually. Between audits, internal verification is carried out by the establishment manager using a standardised checklist.
10. NON-CONFORMANCE AND CORRECTIVE ACTION

Any area found to be in an unacceptable hygiene condition is withdrawn from service. Cleaning is repeated and verified before re-use. All corrective actions are documented and reviewed at the monthly management meeting.
11. ESTABLISHMENT CONDITION ASSESSMENT
Rules s4-6 — establishment to be maintained in a condition appropriate for export operations (C5)

The most recent quarterly hygiene review at Gawler River Almonds (conducted 18 November 2024) confirmed that all areas are maintained in accordance with this Hygiene and Sanitation Plan. No corrective actions outstanding.
